template_name: Hippocampal Relational Binding in Environmental Encoding

mechanism_chain.process: Environmental input — multi-feature spatial configuration (proportion, lighting, materials, acoustic signature, olfactory cues) — enters parahippocampal place area (PPA) via ventral visual stream

data.finding: PPA shows selective activation for spatial scenes, places, and environmental layouts independent of specific objects
PPA → entorhinal → hippocampal pathway transmits spatial scene information for memory encoding

justification.backing: The PPA is the cortical gateway for spatial scene processing. Its selective activation for places and layouts is well-established, and its connectivity to hippocampus via entorhinal cortex provides the anatomical pathway for spatial memory encoding.
justification.qualifier: The PPA-hippocampal pathway is demonstrated; the specific contribution of each feature dimension (proportion, lighting, materials) to PPA encoding is less precisely quantified.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if spatial scene processing bypassed PPA via alternative pathways; but lesion and neuroimaging evidence consistently implicate PPA as necessary for scene encoding.

mechanism_chain.process: DG performs pattern separation on incoming spatial configuration: if distinctiveness exceeds separation threshold (~60–70% dissimilarity to stored patterns in young adults), orthogonal hippocampal representation is created
mechanism_chain.substrate: DG mossy fiber pathway → CA3 recurrent collaterals

data.finding: DG shows pattern separation: similar inputs produce dissimilar outputs; high-resolution fMRI reveals DG/CA3 activity distinguishes similar spatial scenes
Pattern separation threshold increases with age (from ~35% to ~50% dissimilarity required)
data.source: Yassa et al. (2011); Stark et al. (2013)

justification.backing: Yassa and Stark's work established the computational role of DG in pattern separation using high-resolution fMRI. The separation threshold determines whether new spatial inputs create distinct representations or are assimilated to existing patterns.
justification.qualifier: The ~60-70% dissimilarity threshold is derived from laboratory stimuli; translation to architectural feature dimensions involves capacity assumptions about how spatial features are weighted.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if pattern separation in humans operates differently than predicted by computational models; but fMRI evidence supports the DG pattern separation role.

mechanism_chain.process: CA1 binds separated spatial representation with temporal context, emotional valence, and co-present social information into relational episodic trace
mechanism_chain.substrate: CA1 pyramidal neurons; Schaffer collateral input from CA3 + direct EC layer III input

data.finding: CA1 activation during encoding predicts subsequent relational memory (binding of items to context) but not item memory alone
CA1 receives convergent input from CA3 (spatial) and EC layer III (temporal/contextual), enabling relational binding
data.effect: CA1 integrates spatial and temporal information

justification.backing: Davachi's work established CA1 as the site of relational binding in episodic memory. The convergence of CA3 spatial information and EC temporal/contextual information in CA1 provides the neural substrate for integrating what, where, and when.
justification.qualifier: The relational binding function of CA1 is well-established; the specific contribution of architectural context (vs. other contextual information) to the binding is less directly measured.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if relational binding occurred elsewhere in the hippocampal circuit; but lesion and imaging evidence converge on CA1 as the binding site.

mechanism_chain.process: Encoding strength modulated by environmental distinctiveness: more distinctive spatial configurations produce stronger DG separation, more orthogonal CA3 representations, and more durable CA1 relational bindings

data.finding: Novel or distinctive stimuli produce stronger hippocampal activation and better subsequent memory than familiar or generic stimuli
The ~35% encoding strength boost for distinctive vs. generic environments is estimated from hippocampal activation differences
data.source: Panel estimate from Davachi fMRI data

justification.backing: The distinctiveness → encoding strength link follows from the DG pattern separation cascade: more distinctive inputs produce more orthogonal representations, which produce stronger, less interference-prone memory traces.
justification.qualifier: The 35% encoding boost is a panel estimate derived from laboratory novelty effects. Direct measurement of architectural distinctiveness effects on hippocampal encoding is absent.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if encoding strength is determined by attention or emotional salience rather than distinctiveness per se; these factors may co-vary with distinctiveness in real environments.

environmental_novelty_level.interpretation: Adjacent spaces must differ on ≥50% of weighted feature dimensions for DG pattern separation (adults 65+)

visual_complexity.interpretation: Weight distribution across feature dimensions for distinctiveness computation; spatial proportion and lighting weighted highest per PPA encoding priority

hippocampal_encoding.interpretation: Distinctive environments (>threshold dissimilarity) produce ~35% stronger hippocampal encoding than generic environments

age_group.effect: Pattern separation threshold increases from 0.35 to 0.50; encoding strength boost reduced to 1.20
age_group.mechanism: DG neurogenesis decline; perforant path degradation (Small et al., 2011)

clinical_condition.effect: Encoding strength reduced by 15–25% (multiplier 0.75–0.85); interacts with STRESS-I T6 hippocampal volume parameter
clinical_condition.mechanism: Glucocorticoid receptor-mediated suppression of LTP in CA1 (Kim & Diamond, 2002)

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Hippocampal encoding efficiency is modulated by interoceptive state. Body budget deficit (allostatic load > threshold, per IC2) reduces hippocampal LTP capacity and impairs relational binding. The encoding strength parameter should be discounted by IC2's allostatic_load_modifier when body budget is in deficit.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Perceived environmental control modulates encoding through stress pathways. Low perceived control elevates cortisol (AX4 → T6 pathway), which suppresses hippocampal encoding. The encoding strength multiplier should incorporate AX4's control_deficit_cortisol_amplifier as a secondary modifier.

cross_template_references: ED_PATTERN_SEP_COMP_001 — provides the DG separation threshold that gates encoding strength
STRESS-I T6 — cortisol modulation of hippocampal encoding
SPATIAL-I SC1 — spatial integration parameters feed the spatial proportion dimension

visual_complexity.interpretation: Varying ceiling height, room width, or volume between adjacent spaces contributes 0.25 to distinctiveness score per unit of variation

luminance_level.interpretation: Contrast in luminance, color temperature, or directionality between adjacent spaces

material_surface_properties.interpretation: Different floor or wall materials between adjacent spaces
